newsitem.title: CHINA: Guangdong Expressway plans A shares.
newsitem.headline: Guangdong Expressway plans A shares.

text.p: Guangdong Provincial Expressway Development Co Ltd plans to issue 100 million A shares for listing in Shenzhen this year, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission has given the company preliminary approval to make the offer, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.

He said that if successful, the firm would use part of the proceeds to expand its 75 percent-owned four-lane Guangzhou-Foshan highway to six or eight lanes, which entails investment of 200-300 million yuan.
The 15.7-km highway, which opened in 1989, was described by analysts as the most profitable toll road in southern Guangdong province.

The official said the company would put the rest of the proceeds towards the construction of the 105-km Dianbai-Zhanjiang highway in Guangdong province and increase its stake in the Foshan-Kaiping highway to 39 percent from 25 percent.
The firm posted a net profit of 140.13 million yuan for 1996 and 118.48 million yuan in 1995 under international accounting standards.
Based on Chinese standards, it booked net earnings of 137.46 million yuan for last year against 138.40 million yuan in 1995.
Guangdong Expressway had 442.8375 million shares at end-1996, composed of 190.9625 million state shares, 89.6850 million institutional, 27.19 million staff and 135 million B shares.
The B shares were issued at HK$3.54 each last year and were listed in Shenzhen in August.
The company, based in Guangdong's capital Guangzhou, also has 30-year operating rights for the Jiujiang Bridge opened in 1988.
